title: Ohn No Khao Swè
description: Chicken in a coconut broth thickened with toasted chickpea flour, poured over egg noodles. Everything else goes on at the table, which is half the pleasure of it.
notes: The chickpea flour is what separates this from a coconut curry with noodles in it. It gives the broth a nutty body that fat alone never does, and it is the reason the soup clings to the noodles instead of sliding off them.

steps.text: Blend the onions, garlic and ginger to a smooth paste with a splash of water.
Fry the paste in the peanut oil over a medium heat until it has darkened by two shades and no longer smells raw.
steps.tip: This is the longest twelve minutes in the recipe and the one everybody cuts short. Wait until the oil separates out at the edges of the pan.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric and paprika, then add the chicken thighs and turn them until every piece is coated and sealed.
Whisk the chickpea flour into the cold chicken stock until there is not a lump left, then pour it into the pan along with the coconut milk and the fish sauce.
steps.tip: Slurry first, every time. Chickpea flour dropped into hot liquid sets into pellets you will be fishing out all evening.

steps.text: Simmer, stirring now and then, until the soup thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Boil the egg noodles, drain them hard, and divide them between deep bowls.
steps.tip: Drain them properly. Water left clinging to the noodles thins the soup right where you poured it.

steps.text: Ladle the soup over the noodles and let everyone build their own bowl with the eggs, red onion, fried shallots, lime, coriander and chilli flakes.
